title: The Key: three persona builds, one exam
intro: Each of the nine actors gets three different persona cards, built from the same dated record, and the cards are then raced: same questions, scored against what the actor actually did next (see The experiment tab). Where the cards come from: everything starts from actor-persona.pages.dev - the source site. That site holds each actor's dated rows (date, verb, one-line description, quote, source link), a cutoff date, and an analyst-written seven-step persona (Purpose, Standing, Powers, Record, Reactions, Reach, Limits). This project takes the source site's rows and cutoffs, and adds the three test cards, the hidden answer keys, and the comparison. It does not change the source records.

tests.name: Test 1 - The Plain Record
tests.one_line: The agent sees the actor's history word for word: every dated, sourced fact in order, with a one-line identity at the top. Nothing else.
tests.built_from: The dated rows already on actor-persona.pages.dev, plus a new computed menu of the verbs the actor has actually used.
tests.bet: The record itself is the persona - the bet behind the two best results in the field ([Political Actor Agent, AAAI 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07144); [Park et al., Stanford, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.10109)). Anything fancier has to beat this card to justify itself.
tests.exam: Pick the verb for each hidden later action. Scored by exact match against the real action, normalized by the actor's own consistency.

tests.name: Test 2 - The Rule Card
tests.one_line: Instead of every fact, the agent gets a short list of patterns pulled from those facts: when X happened, this actor did Y, by about this much, within this many days.
tests.built_from: Trigger-to-response pairs computed from the dated rows and shared event list, following the site's own protocols (a trigger must be a dated row; gaps are computed, never guessed; three or more episodes make a rule). Sizes come from the record or from cited background research.
tests.bet: A few measured patterns beat a pile of facts, because patterns generalize and facts only describe - the bet behind the only simulation that ever beat standard forecasts ([Wiese et al., Oxford / Farmer group, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18760)).
tests.exam: Same hidden actions as Test 1. A rule fires when its trigger occurs in the question; the prediction is the rule's verb. Scored identically.

tests.name: Test 3 - The Expert Read
tests.one_line: The plain record plus four short readings of it, written once: what a psychologist, an economist, a political scientist, and a domain expert would notice.
tests.built_from: The four readings are written from the pre-cutoff rows only. Every claim uses action words and cites the row it rests on. At question time only the matching reading is attached.
tests.bet: The record says more than it states outright - trained eyes can pull out what it implies; the bet behind the 83%-to-86% lift in [Park et al., Stanford, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.10109), with the action-language rule from [Wang, Lester & Srivastava, 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18566).
tests.exam: Same hidden actions. Only difference from Test 1 is the added lens, so any score gap belongs to the lens.

structure.what: One line: the actor's name and what kind of actor it is.
Every fact with its date, its verb, its wording, and a link to its source, in chronological order.
The verbs this actor has actually used, split into core (used twice or more) and rare (used once). The agent may answer only from this menu.
structure.origin: NEW - the site defines verbs ruled out, but not a per-actor menu of verbs observed

structure.what: Trigger, response, delay (median and range in days), size where the record quantifies it, direction (open or closed), and a stability check.
structure.origin: Partly - the site's reactions step has trigger/response and computed gaps; we add size, direction, stability, and status tiers

structure.what: Psychologist, economist, political scientist, domain expert - each a short reading of the record, every claim citing rows.
structure.origin: NEW - nothing like it in the schema

structure.what: Each topic maps to the one expert reading that answers it, so only that reading is attached per question.
structure.origin: NEW - reuses the site's topic taxonomy

structure.what: The actor's actions dated after its cutoff - each one is an exam question with a known answer (the verb).
structure.origin: NEW - the site stops at the cutoff; we keep the after-cutoff rows as the answer key

structure.what: The site's analyst-written sections: what the persona is for, who can stop the actor, what it can and cannot do, who follows its acts, what we don't know.
structure.origin: Yes - deliberately EXCLUDED from all three prompts so the tests measure the record, not analyst prose

changes.what: Observed action menu (core/rare verbs per actor)
changes.why: The source site rules verbs OUT by power (its Powers step) but never lists what the actor has actually done. We computed that list from the rows, because the exam requires the agent to choose only from actions the actor has really taken.

changes.what: After-cutoff rows kept as a hidden answer key
changes.why: On the source site the cutoff is simply the end of the data. We split instead of dropping: everything dated after the cutoff becomes the exam - 159 questions with known answers.

changes.what: Size, direction, and leave-one-out stability added to rules
changes.why: The source site's Reactions step already records trigger-to-response pairs with computed day gaps (its protocols: a trigger must be a dated row; gaps are computed, never estimated; three-plus episodes make a rule). We kept all of that and added the missing halves: how much (size), which way (direction), and whether the rule survives having any single episode removed.
On the source site, DeepSeek, Huawei, Jensen Huang, MIIT and SAMR had no completed rules (their rule drafts existed as hypotheses). We built their cards from the rows with the same protocols.

changes.what: Four expert readings and topic-to-lens routing
changes.why: Nothing like this exists on the source site - the nearest thing is its analyst narrative, which is excluded from every prompt. The lens layer is new: four readings per actor, written once from pre-cutoff rows, every claim citing the row it rests on.

changes.what: All analyst-written sections excluded from every prompt
changes.why: The source site's Purpose, Standing, Powers, Reach and Limits sections are analyst prose. Leaving them in would contaminate all three arms; excluding them is what makes the comparison about the record.

changes.what: One fixed prompt format per test
changes.why: Identical rendering across actors, so score differences belong to the card, not the formatting.

changes.what: Rule statistics rebuilt from pre-cutoff episodes only
changes.why: Our own fact-check found the first rule build had used 41 episodes dated after the cutoff - rows from the hidden answer key, i.e. the card was partly trained on the exam. Post-cutoff episodes are kept for transparency but no longer count; two rules built entirely after the cutoff were excluded from the exam.

exam: The full comparison - arms, metrics, controls, and the code to run it - is on The experiment tab. Metrics are those of the reference papers: exact action match, consistency-normalized accuracy, macro-F1; IncidentBench's McNemar and bootstrap for comparisons.
footer: Built from the public data at actor-persona.pages.dev (9 actors, 7-step persona build). This site adds the test layers; it does not change the source records.
